## TL;DR

The scheduled-tasks page now uses a compact horizontal card layout with a right-aligned action column, and every shared modal action row has a visibly stronger hover state plus a keyboard focus ring. The delete confirmation keeps its dialog open while the request runs, disables duplicate submits, and shows a failure inline. The capture fixture `agents:scheduledSeeded` is a first-class shot fixture: it seeds rows through `applyShotPreviewFixture`, stamps the applied-state marker a capture probes, and is re-applied after a live schedule fetch so an SSE refresh cannot wipe it mid-capture. The hand-rolled fixed overlays on this page (`RestartTaskDialog`, the schedule editor drawer, the Agents skills modal) are now body-teleported and layer-marked. `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passes on the final tree, with the test suite run by remote validation and the seven targeted suites green locally.

## Work and rationale

- **Cards.** Details stay in the shared `.kv-rows` grid (each row wrapped so its `dt`/`dd` pair aligns), and the three actions sit in a vertical right-hand column. Below 900px the detail block stacks and the actions become a wrapping row, following the Dev page reference. 900px was chosen because the sidebar is still visible down to 761px, where a horizontal row squeezed the value column. The `--kv-label-w` column keeps values aligned instead of letting them wrap under their labels.
- **Dialog interaction.** The delete confirmation already used the shared body-teleported `DeleteConfirmDialog`, so I did not claim that path changed. The genuine common-cause work is the hand-rolled fixed overlays that rendered inline: Radix does not portal `DialogContent`, and an inline fixed layer breaks the shared dismissable-layer ordering, leaving a lower layer with an inline `pointer-events: none` no stylesheet can override. Those three overlays now match the `#0575` rule, and the editor-drawer comment describes that class of bug rather than claiming it was the exact cause of the reported dead buttons. The schedule panel's own delete state moved into explicit handlers (`openDelete`, `setDeleteDialogOpen`, `confirmDeleteSchedule`) so the dialog lifecycle is testable.
- **Action affordance.** The hover rule now uses a 22% `currentColor` wash plus a `currentColor` border instead of a brightness-only change that shifted roughly 5/255 and could not be seen in a screenshot. The same hover and `:focus-visible` treatment covers every modal action row: `.cc-modal-actions`, `.delete-confirm-actions`, `.restart-actions`, `.hotfix-actions`, `.dirty-actions`, `.ste-actions`, and `.stop-work-modal-actions` — table-driven in `overlay-layer-isolation.test.ts` so a new dialog class is added in one place.
- **Delete lifecycle.** Cancel closes without deleting; confirm deletes and closes; a failure renders in the dialog with the dialog still open; a second click while in flight is a no-op. Tests dispatch real `pointerdown`/`pointerup`/`click` events rather than Vue's `.trigger("click")`, so they exercise the same path a mouse takes, and the WebKit test hit-tests both actions above a pointer-disabled drawer and asserts a mean channel shift of at least 8/255 for hover.
- **Capture fixture.** `schedule:seeded` previously seeded rows from inside the panel, which left `data-repoos-shot-state` unset, so a declared state could never verify. It is now `agents:scheduledSeeded`, handled in `applyShotPreviewFixture`, and `refreshSchedules()` re-applies the seed after a live fetch so an SSE `schedule.changed`/`schedule.run` cannot wipe it mid-capture (the same pattern `#0782` uses for board fixtures). The id deliberately avoids the `schedule:` prefix: the capture driver maps that prefix to "a dialog must be open", and that mapping is evaluated by the control-plane build, which may predate this branch. A prefix-safe id needs no cross-build coordination. Three captures are declared: the wide horizontal card with row/action assertions, the delete dialog with Cancel hovered, and a 640px-wide card so the responsive stacking is visible.

## Approaches tried

I first considered making the shared `DialogContent` primitive portal itself, which would fix every caller that forgot a `Teleport`. That is a large behavioural change across many dialogs and tests, so I kept the fix scoped to the hand-rolled layers named above and documented the class instead. For the fixture, I tried a panel-local health watcher first; the store-level re-apply is simpler and matches how other fixtures survive refreshes, so the panel now only fetches normally.

## Challenges and blockers

The original dead-click symptom is not reproducible in the current tree, and the shared delete dialog was already teleported on `main`; I fixed and tested the real sibling instances rather than claiming a reproduction. Keyboard focus has no shot step in the capture vocabulary, so it is covered by the WebKit computed-style assertion (`:focus-visible`, 2px outline on both actions) rather than faked in a screenshot. The WebKit interaction test treats an installed-but-unlaunchable browser as a skip (missing host deps, sandbox) instead of failing the suite.

## Key learnings

A fixture that seeds state outside `applyShotPreviewFixture` cannot satisfy the capture probe even when the screen looks right. Fixtures that seed a live-fetched list also need a re-apply hook on refresh, not just a mount-time seed. A capture fixture's id is also an input to code that may run from a different build than the branch: pick an id whose prefix carries no structural meaning rather than teaching every build a new exception. For dialog affordances, a computed-style assertion is not enough: the hover delta has to be large enough to read in a capture.
